title: Second triangle identity for dualizable evaluation
statement: The second triangle identity in the conclusion of dualizable_evaluation_criterion holds.

proof.text: Specialize the assumed adjunction naturality hadj at eta and identity maps. Apply adj to h_eta and substitute h_phi_def(K). Applying the equivalence to h_eta and using its inverse identities gives lambda_K.hom = (eta tensor id_K);alpha;(id_K tensor e);rho_K.hom. Precompose by lambda_K.inv to obtain the first triangle.

proof.text: Define g to be the displayed D-triangle composite. The proved private helper evaluation_slide identifies (g tensor id_K);e with (id_D tensor first_triangle_composite);e. It is proved by monoidal coherence, followed by Mathlib MonoidalCategory.whisker_exchange(e,e), followed by monoidal coherence. The first triangle therefore gives (g tensor id_K);e=e.

source.place: Tag 0FPC, formal tensor-Hom duality criterion; Tag 0FPB, monoidal constraints

proof.text: Let I be the tensor unit and t=lambda_D.inv;phi_I. Specialize hadj to identity maps in its last two variables. The resulting naturality equation and h_phi_def(I), with monoidal coherence, give adj(D,K,I)(t)=e. Apply this naturality at g and use the evaluation equality to obtain adj(g;t)=adj(t). Injectivity gives g;t=t. Since t is an isomorphism by h_phi(I), cancel t to obtain g=id_D, then take symmetry.
